Saffron Biscotti

Served at: St. Lucia's Day

Makes about 24 biscottiPrep 20 minCook 40 min

Saffron Biscotti are traditional Swedish cookies enjoyed during St. Lucia's Day, a festival celebrated on December 13th to honor Saint Lucia, symbolizing light in the dark winter. The subtle saffron flavor in these crunchy, twice-baked cookies evokes the warmth and festive spirit of this Scandinavian holiday.

Ingredients

  • 2 1/2 cups (310 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground saffron threads, crushed and steeped in 1 tablespoon hot water
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) granulated sugar
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) sliced almonds, toasted

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
  3. In a small bowl, combine crushed saffron with hot water and let steep for 5 minutes.
  4. In a large bowl, beat eggs and sugar until pale and fluffy, about 3-4 minutes.
  5. Add saffron water and vanilla extract to the egg mixture and mix well.
  6. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined.
  7. Fold in the toasted sliced almonds.
  8. Divide dough in half and shape each half into a log about 12 inches (30 cm) long and 2 inches (5 cm) wide. Place logs on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them apart.
  9. Bake for 25-30 minutes, until golden and firm to the touch. Remove from oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
  10. Reduce oven temperature to 300°F (150°C). Using a serrated knife, cut each log diagonally into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thick slices.
  11. Place slices cut side down on the baking sheet and bake for another 10-15 minutes, flipping halfway through, until dry and crisp.
  12. Cool biscotti completely on a wire rack before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the granulated sugar with brown sugar.
  • Add dried cranberries or orange zest for a festive twist.
  • Store biscotti in an airtight container to keep them crisp for up to two weeks.
